draft.title: Features of early societies
card: As early societies grew, they needed ways to organise large numbers of people. Many of them developed similar features.
Tools and writing
Tools made work such as farming and building easier. Writing let people keep records, such as how much grain was stored.
Laws and religion
Laws set rules for how people should behave. Religions shared beliefs and rituals that could bring people together.
Social classes
People were often divided into groups with different levels of power and wealth, such as rulers, workers and farmers.
draft.remember: Tools, writing, laws, religions and classes helped early societies organise many people.

a.q: A ruler in an early city has scribes record how much grain each farmer hands over. Which feature does this show?
opts: Writing used to keep records
Laws used to set punishments
Religion used to share beliefs
Tools used to ease farm work
a.why: Scribes noting down amounts of grain are using writing to keep records. Laws set rules for behaviour, and this scene is about recording, not about rules.
a.clue: What are the scribes doing with the grain amounts?

b.q: In the city of Kalu, a council announces that anyone who steals from a neighbour must repay double. How does this help the city to organise its many people?
opts: It sets shared rules for how people should behave
It divides people into groups of different wealth
It gives people a way to record how much they own
It makes farming and building work easier to do
b.why: A rule about stealing and repayment is a law, and shared rules help many people live together. Social classes sort people by power and wealth, which is a different feature.
b.clue: The council is setting a rule for behaviour.

b.best: It sets shared rules for how people should behave

problems.detail: The clue ('The council is setting a rule for behaviour') nearly repeats the right option ('sets shared rules for how people should behave'), so students can match the words without understanding what laws do.

check.summary: The card and both questions are accurate, but question b's clue almost states the right option word for word. It should be reworded so it hints rather than gives the answer away.

flags: Question b, other: The clue ('The council is setting a rule for behaviour') nearly repeats the right option ('sets shared rules for how people should behave'), so students can match the words without understanding what laws do.
